title: Reconceptualized Associative Learning
identity_check: Opens as Perspectives on Behavior Science 10.1007/s40614-025-00442-8 (PMC12162447) 'Reconceptualized Associative Learning', C. R. Gallistel, Rutgers Center for Cognitive Science - matches the registered R14-N7 title and single authorship.
mapping_note: paper wording 'learning rate ... scalar function of relative temporal separation, as measured by informativeness' -> our K5 delay/memory; 'shortening the ITI ... the number of reinforcements required will increase by more than a factor of 60' -> our K2 inhibition/gate; 'an association is a measurable fact about the distribution of events in time, not an altered activation-conducting connection' -> our K10 role reassignment. Gallistel uses none of the K-family words.
description_scope: Judged under the description 'the number of reinforcements required before a conditioned response appears, as a function of the temporal separation of events'; the paper's own action term is 'deciding to act on' perceived temporal associations, but the D judgement here is about acquisition, not about which action the subject takes.
motion_source: L0 formal carrier: rate-ratio (informativeness) algebra over counted events and measured durations, represented in L2 symbols in memory and read out at L4 as the decision to respond; no new physiological measurement.

mechanism.claim: Learning rate is an almost scalar function of the relative temporal separation of events (informativeness), so wider spacing - not more pairings - buys faster acquisition, and time-scale invariance makes the number of reinforcements the wrong currency.
mechanism.quote: The learning rate—operationally defined as the reciprocal of reinforcements prior to the appearance of a conditioned response—is an almost scalar function of relative temporal separation, as measured by informativeness.

mechanism.claim: Crowding trials collapses informativeness into the region where the learning rate goes to zero, so shortening the ITI raises the reinforcements required more than sixtyfold - a gate on acquisition set by temporal structure.
mechanism.quote: Shortening the intertrial interval to 5 s produces an informativeness of (5 + 5)/5 = 2, which moves the regression in Fig. 4 into the region where it curves upward toward infinity (0 learning rate). Therefore, the number of reinforcements required will increase by more than a factor of 60.

mechanism.claim: The paper reassigns what an association is - a measurable statistical fact about the distribution of events in time rather than a changed connection in a mind, brain or net - and correspondingly denies decaying eligibility traces as its mechanism.
mechanism.quote: Research on the role of time in associative learning has changed our understanding of what an association is. It is a measurable fact about the distribution of events in time, not an altered activation-conducting connection in a mind, brain or net.

event_grammar: [MOTION] cues and reinforcements arrive at measurable conditional and unconditional rates in the environment (L0) --> [GATE] informativeness (cycle-to-trial rate ratio) must be high enough for the perceived temporal association to control behaviour (L0/L4) --> [ACTION] the conditioned response appears after few reinforcements when events are widely spaced / [INACTION] with crowded ITIs acquisition approaches zero however many pairings are given (L4) --> [OUTCOME] a time-scale-invariant symbol of the temporal association is laid down in memory (L2/L4) --> [FEEDBACK] prospective and retrospective rate estimates are continuously re-derived from counts and durations (L0)

anchor_concordance.reason: Extends and partly contradicts: it endorses interval-over-pairings (and cites Burke et al. 2023, the anchor's own preprint, for the eight-fewer-trials/same-training-time isomorphism, so that support is second-hand), but makes the controlling variable the informativeness/C-T ratio rather than the inter-reward interval, and it explicitly denies the eligibility-trace/dopamine mechanization the anchor relies on.

notes: Theory/review article - no new experiments; its support for the cluster is conceptual plus a literature synthesis (Gibbon/Jenkins labs, Gottlieb, Balsam et al.). Two registered divergences from the anchor: (1) 'There are no windows of associability nor decaying eligibility traces' (offset 2192) contradicts the ANCCR trace mechanism the anchor's account requires; (2) it demands a trade-off test for any dopamine linkage hypothesis - 'One reinforcement with high informativeness must produce the same signal as several hundred with low informativeness' (offset ~127900) - and states that no proposed dopamine linkage hypothesis has been given such a test, which is a challenge to, not a confirmation of, the anchor's dopaminergic half. Bears on the K6 side of C-03. Its 'learning rate' is operationally the reciprocal of reinforcements to a conditioned response, which is not the same quantity as the anchor's per-experience acquisition slope.
